# Interaction and click-flow map

<!-- GENERATED by tools/interaction-map.mjs — do not edit by hand. -->
<!-- Edit docs/interaction-tasks.json for task journeys, then run: node tools/interaction-map.mjs -->

This is a source-derived map of the Svelte desktop UI. It counts template controls, traces their handlers through local functions and component callback bindings, and records page, native-command, native-dialog, modal, external-link, and callback destinations. A template control inside an `{#each}` block is counted once; runtime repetition is shown in its guard column.

Static wiring is evidence of the path in source. It is not proof that a native picker, Tauri window, provider, real media run, or conditional branch works at runtime; those limits are called out below.

## Cardinal-rule task paths

The task catalog compares declared candidate paths. `Minimum` is the shortest complete path in the catalog; `+N` marks excess click opportunities. Text entry, native picker choices, scrolling, and waiting are listed as notes but are not counted as clicks. A non-button interaction can declare an explicit `clicks` cost when the task requires a tap, such as a checkbox acknowledgment.

### Add a folder to the media queue

Open the native folder picker, choose a folder, and scan it into the queue.

| Candidate path | Clicks | Delta from minimum | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Home with an empty queue → Add folder | 1 | shortest | mapped |
| Library empty state → Add folder | 1 | shortest | mapped |
| Library queue manager → Add folder | 1 | shortest | mapped |
| YouTube prep → Add folder | 1 | shortest | mapped |

Notes: The picker selection and scan duration are not clicks in this source map.

### Add files to the media queue

Open the native file picker, choose one or more supported video files, and scan them.

| Candidate path | Clicks | Delta from minimum | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Home with an empty queue → Add files | 1 | shortest | mapped |
| Library empty state → Add files | 1 | shortest | mapped |
| Library queue manager → Add files | 1 | shortest | mapped |

### Run an integrity check

Check a scanned selection without writing media output.

| Candidate path | Clicks | Delta from minimum | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Library action → Check integrity | 1 | shortest | mapped |
| Run page → Start quick integrity check | 1 | shortest | mapped |

Notes: The Run-page path assumes the Integrity mode and Quick depth are already selected; the mode and depth selectors are separately mapped.

### Create a metadata-only MKV

Create a validated MKV copy while preserving the source video and reviewing destinations before start.

| Candidate path | Clicks | Delta from minimum | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Library action → Metadata-only MKV → confirm destination | 2 | shortest | mapped |
| Run page → Metadata → create → confirm destination | 3 | +1 | mapped |

Notes: The output preview can add a Back/adjust loop when collisions are found; that branch is intentionally not counted as a happy path.

### Start a full rebuild

Review the output plan, acknowledge the real encode, and start a validated rebuild.

| Candidate path | Clicks | Delta from minimum | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Library action → Rebuild video → acknowledge → start | 3 | shortest | mapped |
| Run page → Rebuild → start → acknowledge → start | 4 | +1 | mapped |

Notes: The acknowledgment is a required checkbox tap and is counted as one explicit click cost; text entry and native output-folder choices are not counted.

### Create a YouTube upload copy

Analyze selected media and create a separate upload copy without replacing the source.

| Candidate path | Clicks | Delta from minimum | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| YouTube page with an existing scan → Create upload copies | 1 | shortest | mapped |
| YouTube page → Add folder → Create upload copies | 2 | +1 | mapped |

### Review and apply a library rename

Preview a reviewed title/episode filename, confirm the validated preview, and apply the rename.

| Candidate path | Clicks | Delta from minimum | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Library → Organize titles → preview → apply → confirm | 4 | shortest | mapped |

Notes: This happy path assumes the title assignment and selection are already complete; provider lookup and conflict-resolution loops are separate work.

### Stop an active run

Stop safely after the active file, or stop immediately after an explicit confirmation.

| Candidate path | Clicks | Delta from minimum | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Active run → Stop after this file | 1 | shortest | mapped |
| Active run → Stop now → confirmation Stop now | 2 | +1 | mapped |

Notes: Safe stop and immediate stop have different safety semantics; the two-click path is not redundant with the one-click safe stop.

## Redundancy and over-tap hotspots

These are not automatically defects. They are places where the same destination or label has multiple entry points and should be compared against the task paths above.

## Evidence and limits

- Source evidence: the Svelte compiler parsed every file under `desktop/src`, and the inventory records the exact file/line for every control.
- Callback evidence: component props are followed through static parent bindings where the component name resolves to a local `.svelte` file.
- Conditional evidence: `guards` show source conditions and loop templates; the report does not claim every branch was rendered.
- Native boundary: `openDialog`, Tauri `invoke`, OS menus, drag/drop, window behavior, provider requests, and real-media execution still require the project’s native acceptance walkthrough.
- Runtime repetition: controls inside queue/card loops are template controls; one card can create many runtime instances, so task testing should measure both per-item and bulk paths.
